title: 2.4 Five Kingdom Classification
description: The five-kingdom classification system and key features of each kingdom

questions.question: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification system?
questions.explanation: Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system in 1969.

questions.question: Which kingdoms are included in the five-kingdom classification system?
questions.explanation: The five kingdoms are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia as proposed by Whittaker.

questions.question: Which kingdom consists of prokaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera contains prokaryotic organisms (bacteria) that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: What type of cell wall do bacteria in Kingdom Monera have?
questions.explanation: Bacteria have cell walls made of peptidoglycan, a polymer of sugars and amino acids, unlike plants (cellulose) or fungi (chitin).

questions.question: Which kingdom includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms such as amoeba and paramecium?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Protista consists mostly of unicellular eukaryotic organisms like amoeba, paramecium, and euglena.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms belongs to Kingdom Protista?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryotic protist. E. coli is a bacterium (Monera), mushroom is a fungus (Fungi), and oak tree is a plant (Plantae).

questions.question: Algae are classified under which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Although algae can photosynthesize, they are placed in Kingdom Protista because they are simple, mostly unicellular or colonial organisms without true roots, stems, or leaves.

questions.question: Which kingdom includes organisms that are heterotrophic and absorb nutrients through external digestion?
questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic organisms that secrete enzymes externally onto organic matter and absorb the digested nutrients.

questions.question: What is the cell wall of fungi made of?
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin, the same tough substance found in the exoskeleton of insects.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in baking and brewing. Spirulina is a cyanobacterium (Monera), Euglena and Paramecium are protists.

questions.question: Members of Kingdom Plantae are characterized by being:
options: Autotrophic, multicellular, and having cell walls of cellulose
questions.correctAnswer: Autotrophic, multicellular, and having cell walls of cellulose
questions.explanation: Plants are multicellular autotrophs with cellulose cell walls that photosynthesize to produce their own food.

questions.question: Which kingdom includes organisms that are multicellular, heterotrophic, and capable of movement?
questions.explanation: Animals are multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that can move at some stage of their life cycle.

questions.question: Bacteria in Kingdom Monera reproduce mainly by:
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission, where one cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Kingdom Fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi cannot photosynthesize because they lack chlorophyll; they obtain nutrients by absorbing organic matter.

questions.question: Paramecium moves using which structure?
questions.explanation: Paramecium is a protist that moves by beating tiny hair-like structures called cilia.

questions.question: Amoeba moves and feeds using:
questions.explanation: Amoeba uses pseudopodia (false feet) for both movement and engulfing food through phagocytosis.

questions.question: Mushrooms and molds are classified under which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms and molds are both members of Kingdom Fungi, characterized by heterotrophic absorption nutrition and chitin cell walls.

questions.question: Which kingdom contains organisms that can be both autotrophic (photosynthetic) and heterotrophic?
questions.explanation: Some protists like Euglena can photosynthesize (autotrophic) when light is available and become heterotrophic in darkness.

questions.question: What is the main characteristic that distinguishes Kingdom Animalia from Kingdom Plantae?
options: Animals are heterotrophic and capable of movement
questions.correctAnswer: Animals are heterotrophic and capable of movement
questions.explanation: Animals are heterotrophic (cannot make their own food) and most can move, while plants are autotrophic and generally sessile.

questions.question: Which kingdom includes organisms that are all unicellular prokaryotes?
questions.explanation: All members of Kingdom Monera are unicellular prokaryotes, lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: Euglena is classified under Kingdom Protista because it:
options: Has both plant-like and animal-like characteristics
Has chitin in its cell wall
questions.correctAnswer: Has both plant-like and animal-like characteristics
questions.explanation: Euglena has chloroplasts (plant-like) but also moves and feeds heterotrophically (animal-like), placing it in Protista.

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms contains organisms that are primarily decomposers?
questions.explanation: Fungi are the primary decomposers in ecosystems, breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients.

questions.question: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) were formerly classified as algae but are now placed in:
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic bacteria that perform photosynthesis, so they belong to Kingdom Monera, not Protista.

questions.question: Which kingdom has no cell wall at all?
questions.explanation: Animal cells lack cell walls, unlike plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin), and bacteria (peptidoglycan).

questions.question: The mode of nutrition in Kingdom Plantae is:
questions.explanation: Plants are autotrophs that use chlorophyll to convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.
